name: Battle of Okinawa
note: This plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: the formations are armies, corps and divisions, and the ground is the island. Only some of the units are drawn, and the island's outline is schematic. The accounts do not say where the American divisions lay offshore before the landing, so they are placed off the Hagushi beaches; the Thirty-Second Army is placed at Shuri, where its defences lay.

phases.title: The Kerama Islands are taken
phases.text: Soldiers of the 77th Infantry Division landed in the Kerama Islands, 15 miles west of Okinawa. Task Force 58 lay to the east of the island, the Thirty-Second Army held the south and Udo Force the north.
phases.quote: The first Americans ashore were soldiers of the 77th Infantry Division who landed in the Kerama Islands, 15 mi (24 km) west of Okinawa on 26 March.

phases.title: The main landing at the Hagushi beaches
phases.text: The XXIV Corps and the III Amphibious Corps landed on the Hagushi beaches on the west coast. Off the Minatoga beaches in the south-east the 2nd Marine Division made a demonstration to deceive the Japanese.
phases.quote: The main landing was made by the XXIV Corps and the III Amphibious Corps on the Hagushi beaches on the western coast of Okinawa on 1 April.

phases.title: The Marines close the north and the 77th takes Ie Shima
phases.text: The 6th Marine Division sealed off the Motobu Peninsula, where Udo Force was cornered around Mount Yaedake, and cleared it on 18 April. The 77th Division assaulted Ie Shima on 16 April.
phases.quote: By this point, the bulk of the Japanese forces in the north (codenamed Udo Force) were cornered on the Motobu Peninsula.

phases.title: The advance south meets Kakazu Ridge
phases.text: The 96th and 7th Infantry Divisions wheeled south and met Japanese soldiers in fortified caves at Kakazu Ridge, part of Shuri's outer defences. The advance went on, with heavy casualties on both sides.
phases.quote: The American advance was inexorable but resulted in a high number of casualties on both sides.

phases.title: Ushijima attacks across the front
phases.text: Ushijima, influenced by General Chō, took the offensive and the Thirty-Second Army attacked American positions across the whole front on the evening of 12 April. The assaults of the following nights were repulsed.
phases.quote: On the evening of 12 April, the 32nd Army attacked American positions across the entire front.

phases.title: Shuri is left and the army withdraws south
phases.text: The 6th Marine Division occupied the ruins of Naha, and Marines of the 1st Marine Division took Shuri Castle on 29 May, which the Thirty-Second Army had left. The army moved nearly 30,000 men to the Kiyan Peninsula.
phases.quote: The 32nd Army was able to move nearly 30,000 personnel into its last defense line on the Kiyan Peninsula

phases.title: The last pocket in the south
phases.text: Elements of the 6th Marine Division landed on the Oroku Peninsula, and the naval troops died by suicide in their tunnels on 13 June. By 17 June the rest of the Thirty-Second Army was in a small pocket in the far south.
phases.quote: By 17 June, the remnants of Ushijima's shattered 32nd Army were pushed into a small pocket in the far south of the island to the southeast of Itoman.
